title: Force diagram sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 47 (Force diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 47: Balanced and unbalanced forces. To understand how balanced and unbalanced forces affect an object's motion

picture.draw: Draw and label: Force diagram sheet

model.title: A boat: engine 800 N forwards, drag 500 N backwards. Find the resultant and describe the motion.

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Direction of the bigger force: forwards

questions.q: A cyclist: pedal force 150 N, air resistance 90 N. Resultant?
questions.model: Opposite directions, so subtract: 150 - 90 = 60. Bigger force is forwards. 60 N forwards.

questions.q: What happens if air resistance becomes 150 N?
Two people push a box the same way with 30 N and 40 N. Resultant?
Draw force diagrams and find the resultant for four cases (portal sheet): a lorry, a skydiver, a book on a table, a car braking.
questions.a: Lorry: 2000 - 1500 = 500 N forwards; skydiver: 700 - 700 = 0 (steady); book: 0; car: 3000 N backwards (slowing)
questions.model: Teacher draws the lorry: 2000 N forward arrow, 1500 N backward arrow, resultant 500 N forwards.

questions.q: A skydiver opens the parachute. Explain what happens to the forces and speed.
questions.a: Air resistance becomes bigger than weight, so the resultant is upwards and they slow down until forces balance again.

questions.q: Why does a car need a bigger driving force to keep a steady speed at 70 mph than at 30 mph?
questions.a: Drag is much bigger at higher speed, so a bigger force is needed to balance it.

questions.q: Balanced forces on a moving object: it...
Big question: how can a car move steadily with balanced forces?
questions.a: Balanced forces mean no change in motion, so it keeps its speed.
